annotation.title_clean: Legal implications of violating robots.txt: contract and tort liability for web robot behaviour in common law jurisdictions
annotation.title_en: Legal implications of violating robots.txt: contract and tort liability for web robot behaviour in common law jurisdictions
annotation.summary_en: Journal article arguing that violating robots.txt, a voluntary web-crawler exclusion standard, can create civil liability in common law jurisdictions. It contends that robots.txt may form a unilateral contract or serve as notice grounding negligence, as a response to generative-AI scraping. 'Robots' here are software crawlers, not physical robots.
key_provisions_or_claims: robots.txt can operate as a unilateral contract, accepted by the bot deployer's conduct
robots.txt can serve as notice establishing tortious liability, including trespass to chattels and negligence
Civil doctrines are preferable to criminal or copyright remedies for regulating web robots
Clarifying liability is needed to counter fragmentation of the internet caused by AI scraping
Empirical analysis of top 200 websites shows growing blocking of LLM-training crawlers
